text: {"answer": "The evidence suggests intermittent fasting produces weight loss, but it is not clearly superior to standard calorie restriction. A systematic review of 27 trials found weight loss of 0.8% to 13.0% of baseline weight with no serious adverse events, and twelve studies comparing it with calorie restriction found equivalent results [e21d56f2e070#1][f781c705b786#2]. The Harvard Nutrition Source notes that research does not consistently show intermittent fasting is superior to continuous low-calorie diets, and a one-year trial of 100 obese individuals found it no more effective than daily calorie restriction [44e3472ec92d#2][44e3472ec92d#7]. Dropout rates were not lower than for continuous restriction [44e3472ec92d#6]. Small trials combining fasting with calorie restriction reported greater weight loss in obese women [23334c40ad6b#1]. The review authors caution that studies have been small and short, and longer-term research is needed [e21d56f2e070#2]. Wikipedia's summary calls the evidence preliminary, and notes long-term sustainability has not been studied [13ed85eb2cce#6].", "confidence": 72, "one_line": "Intermittent fasting produces modest weight loss comparable to daily calorie restriction, but long-term evidence is limited and it is not clearly superior."}
